# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

I can see the bomb’s current state: display `0`, a yellow light, and three wires in order green, yellow, blue. I cannot interpret the gestures without an agreed code, so I will plainly report the visible details to the Blind and Mute. The Blind can use the physical layout while the Mute checks the manual for the correct procedure.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="I see display 0. The light is yellow. Wires from 1 to 3 are green, yellow, blue. Use the manual's instructions for this configuration.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0. The light is yellow. Wires from 1 to 3 are green, yellow, blue. Please find the manual procedure and tell Blind what to do.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb now shows display `0` with an orange light; the wires remain green, yellow, blue in positions 1–3. The mute’s gesture has no established meaning to me, so I should not infer an instruction from it. I will report the changed light and ask the manual-reader to relay the required action to the Blind.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display remains 0; light is now orange. Wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I cannot interpret the mute's gesture.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0, light changed to orange; wires remain green, yellow, blue. Please check whether the manual gives an action for this state and relay it to Blind.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋ ☝]

The bomb now shows display `0` with a green light; the wire colors are unchanged: green, yellow, blue. The mute’s three gestures still have no agreed meaning, so I will not treat them as an instruction. I’ll send the latest state to both teammates and urge the mute to give the Blind the manual-based action in speech.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0, light now green, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. The mute sent three gestures, but I cannot interpret them.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0, light now green, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please state the manual's required action directly to Blind in speech.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The previous turn was rejected because `🤷` is not in the permitted gesture alphabet. I will resend the bomb state to Blind and ask Mute to communicate the manual’s instruction to Blind by speech. I will omit any gesture.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0; light is yellow again; wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute made one upward-pointing gesture, but its meaning is unconfirmed; do not act on it.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 blue. Please state the manual's required action directly to Blind in speech.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤘]

The bomb remains at display `0`, with the light changing back to orange; wire colors and positions are unchanged. I can see gestures from both teammates, but their meanings have not been established. I will continue relaying the exact state and ask Mute to give Blind the manual’s instruction verbally.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0; light is orange; wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I saw your three gestures, but I cannot determine their meaning.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0, orange light, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 blue. Blind made three gestures to me, but I cannot determine their meaning. Please read the manual and tell Blind the exact action by speech.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb still shows display `0`, and the light is now green. The wires remain, in order, green, yellow, blue. I can see one gesture from each teammate, but gestures have no established meaning here. I will report the updated state and again direct Mute to communicate the manual’s exact instruction to Blind by speech.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0; light is green; wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I see one gesture from you and one from Mute, but neither has an established meaning.")
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0, green light, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 blue. Please read the manual and tell Blind the exact required action by speech; gestures are not sufficient.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The mute cannot speak, so the gestures are their only direct channel to me. I should not call them meaningless; I can relay a literal description to the Blind, who can hear my speech. The bomb currently shows display `0`, yellow light, and wires green, yellow, blue. The Mute signaled one upward-pointing index finger.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signaled one gesture: an index finger pointing upward. Treat this as the mute's manual-derived instruction, if our agreed gesture code identifies it.")
```
